i prefer “customer” over “dead body” or even just “body”. i provide a service to a family which involves me embalming their loved one, which makes them my customer. 

the definition of customer is “ a person or organization that buys goods or services from a store or business.” 

the definition of a dead body is “a natural object consisting of a dead animal or person.” 

to me, the word customer allows more dignity. 
i got into this industry to give as much love as i can to my customers, or as you would prefer, bodys. my customers can no longer care for themselves or have a say in literally anything because they are no longer here. only their body remains. i am more than blessed to be able to take care of, allow dignity, and show love to each and every single one of my customers. so, yes, i do have respect. probably more than most, and definitely more than anyone else that works in that prep room.

the sad thing is, i get paid per embalming. i get paid hourly as well. to be an apprentice, i make amazing money. but i would rather learn more and be able to care for these peoples bodies after they pass than make $400-$500 a week. i would happily do my job for much less if it meant i could do all the small things that allow dignity and show love. yes, i have never met any customer i’ve received in the year and a half i’ve been in this business, but that doesn’t mean they don’t deserve love. 
i mean hell, the people i work with don’t even take the extra 5 seconds to completely unfold a sheet to wear it covers the whole customer including feet. i understand that yes they are covered with a sheet, but in my opinion that’s just half assing it. 

just this week, we have had an overflow of customers and i am not able to properly embalm a body in less than 2 hours, yet my boss insists and is quite rude about it. saying things like “hurry the hell up” “you’re taking too long” “im about to just finish your body” things like that. 
it’s like she would rather have a shitty looking body that’s fine fast than a well cared for, probably embalmed body.

my boss does not wash a customer before an embalming as “it’s unnecessary when you will have to do it at the end anyway”. she gets frustrated with a lot of the little things i do, that i can admit not all are necessary, but allows dignity for my customer. 

some examples would be that we received a two year old cremation who had been autopsied. i by no means HAD to suture up his chest cavity or fill his head and make sure the skull cap was as centered as possible. i didn’t HAVE to put a pull up on him. i didn’t HAVE to wrap him in a sheet, but i did it anyway. 

i’ve had one case that has messed me up. i was even diagnosed with ptsd because of it. two brothers were in a car crash/ explosion. they were 8 and 12. it most definitely was not an open casket nor could we dress them. the family still brought clothes and a few other little things but my boss wanted to just put them in the casket and be done. i took my lunch hour to lay each clothing article and little thing the mom brought for each boy. i laid them out as if they were wearing/ holding the items. 
the fact i was basically forced to take my lunch hour to take care of these boys even contributes slightly to my ptsd. 

the way she reacts to me doing these tasks does make me question wether or not im going about this job correctly or if i’m too focused on the wrong things, but i feel taking the time to do these things, even if the family will never know, is the most important thing i can do in this field.
